name: Grief & Loss
overview: Scripture portrays grief and loss as deeply human experiences, vividly illustrated through the mourning of Abraham for Sarah and Jacob for Joseph, who both rent their clothes and wept openly. These passages reveal the profound sorrow felt at the death or loss of loved ones, emphasizing the legitimacy of mourning and the refusal to be comforted in the face of such pain. The detailed expressions of grief, including wearing sackcloth and widow's garments, underscore the biblical recognition of sorrow as a natural response to loss.
